summary: SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Macro-only, like <climits>. Fills the C11 set C++17 adopted -- the *_DECIMAL_DIG, *_TRUE_MIN and *_HAS_SUBNORM families -- from GCC/Clang builtins where the platform header predates C++17. Where no builtin exists (MSVC) a missing macro STAYS MISSING and is #ifdef-testable: a wrong DBL_TRUE_MIN would be far worse than an absent one, since it would silently misjudge every subnormal comparison written against it. Two silent traps documented on their rows: *_MIN is the smallest positive NORMAL value, not the smallest positive value (for double the two differ by sixteen orders of magnitude), and FLT_ROUNDS is not a constant expression.

CORE SHIPPED 2026-08-25. 28 of 38 catalogued symbol groups, across 21 granular headers plus the umbrella: duration, time_point, the three clocks, duration_cast and time_point_cast, the C++17 rounding set, is_clock and the literals. std::chrono is itself C++11, so there is no back-port win on the core types; what re_std adds is one behaviour across compilers -- including an HONEST steady_clock::is_steady, which reports false rather than claiming steadiness while reading a clock that jumps. Ahead of std: floor / ceil / round / abs (C++17), is_clock and days / weeks / months / years and sys_time (C++20) all back-ported to C++11, and the duration and time_point mutators constexpr from C++14 where std waited for C++17. The time source is the only platform code in the library -- three compile-time tiers (POSIX clock_gettime, C++17 timespec_get, then std::time at one-second resolution), reported by D_RE_STD_CLOCK_SOURCE, with an unsupportable forced choice demoted rather than allowed to error. TRAP TO KNOW: days, months and years are FIXED-LENGTH durations, so t + years(1) advances by the mean Gregorian year, not to the same date next year. The calendar and time-zone surface is a separate entry.

SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Macro-only module: contributes NO re_std:: symbols, because macros have no namespace. Its contribution is availability -- the C++11 LLONG_MIN / LLONG_MAX / ULLONG_MAX set is recovered from the compiler's own __LONG_LONG_MAX__ builtin where the platform header predates it, which is a re-derivation rather than a guess. LLONG_MIN is derived as -LLONG_MAX - 1, never written as a literal (the token -9223372036854775808 is a unary minus on a literal too large to be signed). Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded, so a complete platform header is never overridden. numeric_limits<T> remains the better answer outside preprocessor conditionals.

SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 11 catalogued symbols across 7 granular headers plus the umbrella. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 40-odd symbols across 8 family headers plus the umbrella, catalogued as 13 rows. summary: Phase C6 — the only remaining work after Phases C1-C5 shipped 2026-05-17 (all 17 catalogued symbols delivered). C6 covers the floating-point special case in the strong_order / weak_order niebloids: per [cmp.alg], for `float`, `double`, `long double` inputs the niebloid must produce a deterministic total order even across NaN (treating NaN as ordered relative to all finite values, distinguishing +NaN from -NaN, distinguishing -0 from +0). The standard's algorithm operates on the bit pattern; implementations typically use bit_cast (C++20+) or memcpy. Deferred because the rest of the module is functionally complete without it — FP inputs currently route through path (c) of the niebloid and return their built-in partial_ordering, which fails to convert to strong/weak ordering for NaN (compile or runtime mismatch).
blockers: Per-platform IEEE-754 sign-and-bit-pattern manipulation, ideally via re_std::bit_cast (not yet shipped) or std::memcpy.

summary: Foundational concept library: same_as, derived_from, convertible_to, common_reference_with, common_with, integral, floating_point, signed_integral, unsigned_integral, assignable_from, swappable, destructible, constructible_from, default_initializable, move_constructible, copy_constructible, equality_comparable(_with), totally_ordered(_with), movable, copyable, semiregular, regular, invocable, regular_invocable, predicate, relation, equivalence_relation, strict_weak_order.
blockers: C++20 concept syntax for true concept-form versions; pre-C++20 back-port as SFINAE traits is feasible (re_std already has the foundations in <type_traits>).

summary: coroutine_traits, coroutine_handle, noop_coroutine, suspend_never, suspend_always. Compiler-magic — depends on the coroutine state machine the compiler generates around co_await / co_yield / co_return.
blockers: Compiler must support C++20 coroutines (-fcoroutines on GCC, /await on MSVC). The library half is small; the language half is the constraint.

summary: stacktrace_entry, basic_stacktrace, stacktrace = basic_stacktrace<allocator<stacktrace_entry>>. C++23. Heavily platform-dependent — needs DWARF/PDB symbolisation or the libbacktrace / libunwind path.
blockers: Platform unwinder (libunwind / Windows DbgHelp); symbol resolution table; <format> for formatter<stacktrace_entry> specialisation.

tzdata source for the zone database and the leap-second table; re_std::basic_string for zone names; <format> and <locale> for the formatter specialisations, parse and from_stream; <ostream> for the duration and time_point stream operators.
summary: NOT STARTED. The half of <chrono> the core deliberately left out: the C++20 civil calendar (year, month, day, weekday, year_month_day and the rest -- roughly thirty types, about forty operator/ overloads for the y/m/d syntax, hh_mm_ss and the civil-calendar algorithms), the utc / tai / gps / file clock family with clock_cast and leap seconds, and time_zone / zoned_time / tzdb. Split from the core entry because it is a separate module's worth of work with a separate blocker set, not a loose end. THE CIVIL CALENDAR IS DEFERRED, NOT BLOCKED -- it needs nothing that has not shipped, and could be written against the existing duration and sys_days. It was held back because a PARTIAL calendar is worse than none: a year_month_day that is right about leap years and wrong about the Gregorian reform is a bug that reaches production. Same call as <bitset>'s string constructor. THE ZONE HALF IS GENUINELY BLOCKED, and on a deployment dependency rather than a coding problem: zone rules and the leap-second table are DATA that changes several times a year, and a utc_clock without the table is wrong by exactly the 27 seconds it exists to account for. ONE EXISTING DECISION MUST BE REVISITED WHEN THIS LANDS: the shipped operator""d and operator""y are the duration forms (days, years); in C++20 those suffixes are also the calendar's day and year, so 15d and 2020y become ambiguous and the literals will need splitting by context.

complex<T>, full arithmetic + transcendental support (exp, log, sqrt, sin/cos/tan + hyperbolic + inverse variants), operator<< / operator>>. Medium surface; complex<float/double/long double> specialisations may use compiler builtins.
blockers: <cmath> for the transcendentals; <iostream> for stream operators (which can be deferred).

summary: Engines (linear_congruential_engine, mersenne_twister_engine, subtract_with_carry_engine, the named typedefs mt19937 etc., random_device); adaptors (discard_block_engine, independent_bits_engine, shuffle_order_engine); distributions (uniform_int/real, bernoulli, binomial, geometric, negative_binomial, poisson, exponential, gamma, weibull, extreme_value, normal, lognormal, chi_squared, cauchy, fisher_f, student_t, discrete, piecewise_constant, piecewise_linear); seed_seq, generate_canonical. Large.
blockers: <limits>, <type_traits>; for random_device, a platform entropy source.

summary: valarray<T>, slice / gslice, slice_array / gslice_array / mask_array / indirect_array, transcendentals on valarrays. Specialised; rarely used but still in the standard.

PARTLY DONE. Remediation of a wrong premise. Six modules shipped on 2026-08-25 behind whole-file C++11 gates, justified by the claim that 'core/djinterp.hpp hard-errors below C++11, so C++98 is not a reachable tier'. THE CLAIM IS FALSE: djinterp.hpp contains nothing that hard-errors at C++98 (only an anonymous variadic macro in D_NOEXCEPT_IF and _Pragma in the long-long diagnostic pair, both warnings at most), and RE_STD_AGENT_README states re_std compiles on C++98 through C++26, with a macro table that degrades every C++11 feature and a review checklist of explicit C++98 idioms. ALREADY FIXED: <climits> and <cfloat> were never gated; <cstdlib> has been ungated per-symbol and now reaches C++98; size_t / ptrdiff_t / offsetof / NULL always did; <cstdint> now reaches C++98 through dstdint.h, re_std's own <stdint.h> (2026.10.02; every family under ISO strict C++98 on LP64, the 64-bit ones absent where the ABI makes them `long long`). REMAINING, each a real back-port rather than a gate removal: (1) re_std::byte and its thirteen operations need the struct-wrapper idiom the checklist prescribes for enum class; (2) nullptr_t and max_align_t are genuinely C++11-only and should stay gated -- they are language constructs, not library ones.

NOT STARTED. std::chrono is C++11, which makes a C++98 duration and time_point exactly the kind of back-port this library exists for -- and the largest single coverage win still available in the module. The core needs no C++11 feature: duration is a class template over a ratio, and D_CONSTEXPR already degrades to nothing. What must change: constexpr disappears (so the special values become static member functions returning by value rather than constant expressions); the literals go, since user-defined literals are C++11; the defaulted/deleted members need the private-undeclared idiom; and is_clock needs a void_t substitute. Estimated at roughly the size of the original core. Shipped 2026-08-25 gated on C++11 under the false premise recorded in the entry at priority 41.

basic_string<CharT, Traits, Allocator>, the four char specialisations (string / wstring / u8string (C++20) / u16string / u32string), char_traits<CharT> per-char-type, std::stoX number parsers, std::to_string, the C++17 std::string_view interop, operator+ overloads, hash<string>. Large core component.
blockers: <memory> for allocator; <iterator>; <functional> hash for the hash specs; <limits>.

summary: to_chars / from_chars + chars_format enum. C++17 fast numeric ↔ string conversion (locale-independent). Performance-critical; the integer paths are simple but the FP paths (Ryu / Dragonbox) are substantial.

NOT STARTED. 100 headers exist under re_std/<module>/ but are NOT included by their module umbrella, so `#include <re_std/x>` does not surface them. Some are legitimately internal (optional_base, func_storage, searcher_detail, literal_zero_helper, sp_control_block); most are not. Worst offenders: iterator (33 -- including advance, distance, next, prev, begin/end, reverse_iterator and every iterator tag), functional (13), optional (10, now fixed), ranges (9), exception (8, including terminate and exception_ptr), memory (5), utility (5, now 4), any (4 -- any_cast, make_any, bad_any_cast). THIS IS THE LARGEST SOURCE OF CATALOGUE ERROR IN THE PROJECT: it produces under-reported coverage, since the JSON marks a symbol unimplemented when the code exists and works. Fixing optional and utility this way took minutes each and shipped 11 catalogued symbols. Detection: for each module, list *.hpp and grep the umbrella for each basename.

format / format_to / format_to_n / formatted_size / vformat, format_string, format_args, basic_format_arg, basic_format_context, formatter<T> per-type specs (arithmetic / strings / chrono / ranges / pointers / etc.). Large. Anchor for <print> and <chrono> formatters.
blockers: <string_view>, <string>, <utility>; type-erased visitor for format_args; <charconv> for the numeric paths.

summary: polymorphic_allocator<T>, memory_resource ABC, new_delete_resource / null_memory_resource / get_default_resource / set_default_resource, pool_options, unsynchronized_pool_resource / synchronized_pool_resource / monotonic_buffer_resource. Pmr namespace.
scoped_allocator_adaptor<OuterAlloc, InnerAllocs...>. Niche but standardised — propagates inner allocator to nested containers.
Extended floating-point types: float16_t, float32_t, float64_t, float128_t, bfloat16_t. C++23. Some require compiler / ABI support and may be conditionally absent (_Float16, __bf16, etc.).

vector<T, Alloc> + vector<bool> specialisation, hash<vector<bool>>, comparisons (incl. operator<=>), erase / erase_if free functions. Anchor container — many other modules implicitly need it (e.g. ranges::to default target).
deque<T, Alloc>, comparisons, erase / erase_if. Block-of-blocks layout — implementation is more involved than vector.
list<T, Alloc>, comparisons, erase / erase_if. Doubly-linked list, splice / merge / sort / unique / remove / remove_if / reverse.
forward_list<T, Alloc>, comparisons, erase / erase_if. Singly-linked list (C++11).
stack<T, Container=deque<T>> container adaptor. Trivial wrapper.
queue<T, Container=deque<T>>, priority_queue<T, Container=vector<T>, Compare=less<T>>. Container adaptors.
blockers: <deque>, <vector>, <functional> (for less and the heap algorithms — already in <algorithm>).

summary: map<Key, T, Compare, Alloc> + multimap. Red-black-tree based. Insertion / lookup / range erase / structured-binding-friendly iterators (key, value pair).
set<Key, Compare, Alloc> + multiset. Same tree backbone as <map> but key-only.
unordered_map<Key, T, Hash, KeyEqual, Alloc> + unordered_multimap. Hash-table based.
blockers: <memory>, <iterator>, <utility> for pair, <functional> for hash and equal_to.

summary: unordered_set<Key, Hash, KeyEqual, Alloc> + unordered_multiset.
flat_map<Key, T, Compare, KeyContainer, MappedContainer> + flat_multimap. C++23 — sorted-vector-of-pairs adaptor; cache-friendly alternative to <map>.
flat_set<Key, Compare, KeyContainer> + flat_multiset. C++23 — sorted-vector adaptor; cache-friendly alternative to <set>.
mdspan<T, Extents, LayoutPolicy, AccessorPolicy>, extents, dextents, layout_left / layout_right / layout_stride, default_accessor. C++23 multi-dimensional non-owning view.
inplace_vector<T, N>. C++26 fixed-capacity vector with inline storage. Smaller surface than <vector> but with C++26's deducing-this and constexpr support.
hive<T, Alloc>. C++26 (formerly colony). Bucketed container with stable iterators across insertion / erasure. New design.

std::locale, facet ABC, the named facets (collate, ctype, codecvt, numpunct, num_get/put, money_get/put, time_get/put, messages, money_punct), use_facet / has_facet. Locale-aware character conversion + numeric / time formatting. Large.
blockers: <string>; platform locale database (the C locale at minimum).

summary: codecvt_utf8 / codecvt_utf16 / codecvt_utf8_utf16 specialisations + codecvt_mode. DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++26. Implement only for backward compat if at all.

basic_regex<CharT, Traits>, regex / wregex typedefs, regex_match / regex_search / regex_replace / regex_iterator / regex_token_iterator, match_results / sub_match, regex_constants, regex_error, the regex_traits<CharT> trait. Significant — the parser + NFA/DFA engine is the bulk of the work.

filesystem::path, directory_entry, directory_iterator / recursive_directory_iterator, file_status, perms, file_type, the filesystem free functions (canonical, absolute, copy / copy_file, create_directory, current_path, exists, file_size, hard_link_count, is_*, last_write_time, permissions, read_symlink, remove / remove_all, rename, resize_file, space, status, symlink_status, temp_directory_path, weakly_canonical), filesystem_error.
Forward declarations for the iostream subsystem. Tiny — just the templated typedef chain that lets you forward-declare std::ostream et al without dragging in <iostream>.
ios_base, basic_ios, fmtflags / iostate / openmode / seekdir / streamoff / streampos, manipulators (boolalpha, showpoint, etc.). Foundational for the whole I/O subsystem.
basic_streambuf<CharT, Traits>. The buffer ABC that every iostream sits on. Virtual interface; concrete derived buffers live in <fstream>, <sstream>, <syncstream>, <spanstream>.
basic_istream<CharT, Traits>, basic_iostream<CharT, Traits>, operator>> overloads for the arithmetic types and std::string, ws / getline manipulators.
basic_ostream<CharT, Traits>, operator<< overloads for the arithmetic types and std::string, endl / ends / flush / emit_on_flush / noemit_on_flush / flush_emit manipulators.
The global standard streams: cin / cout / cerr / clog and their wide cousins. Static-init order is delicate (the Schwarz counter pattern).
blockers: <istream>, <ostream>; freestanding-mode behaviour needs platform glue (write(2) / WriteFile).

summary: basic_filebuf, basic_ifstream / basic_ofstream / basic_fstream. The disk-backed stream family.
basic_stringbuf, basic_istringstream / basic_ostringstream / basic_stringstream. String-backed streams; common for parsing and formatting.

Parametric manipulators: setbase, setfill, setprecision, setw, setiosflags, resetiosflags, get_time / put_time, get_money / put_money, quoted (C++14). Tiny — each manipulator is a small expression-template.
basic_osyncstream / basic_syncbuf. C++20 — wraps an underlying stream and atomically emits on destruction. Synchronises concurrent writes.
basic_spanstream and basic_spanbuf. C++23 — span-backed stream (alternative to stringstream for fixed-buffer use cases).
std::print / std::println / std::vprint_unicode / std::vprint_nonunicode. C++23 — std::format-based formatted I/O, the closest std equivalent to printf.
blockers: <format>; platform Unicode-stdout detection (IsConsole + GetConsoleMode on Windows).

summary: strstream / istrstream / ostrstream / strstreambuf. DEPRECATED since C++98 — superseded by <sstream>. Include only for backwards compat.

std::atomic<T> + std::atomic_flag, the full operation surface (load / store / exchange / compare_exchange_weak/strong / fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor / wait/notify_one/notify_all (C++20)), memory_order enum, atomic_ref<T> (C++20), atomic<shared_ptr<T>> + atomic<weak_ptr<T>> (C++20). Anchor for lock-free programming and the <memory> Phase 6d follow-ups.
blockers: Compiler intrinsics (__atomic_* / __c11_atomic_* / std::atomic builtins); platform memory model.

summary: std::thread, std::jthread (C++20), this_thread:: namespace (get_id / sleep_for / sleep_until / yield), thread::id and its hash, hardware_concurrency. Foundational for the rest of concurrency.
blockers: Platform thread creation (pthread / Win32); <stop_token> for jthread; <chrono> for sleep_*.

summary: mutex / recursive_mutex / timed_mutex / recursive_timed_mutex, lock_guard / unique_lock / scoped_lock (C++17), once_flag / call_once, try_lock, std::lock (variadic). Pervasive.
blockers: Platform mutex (pthread_mutex_t / CRITICAL_SECTION); <chrono> for the timed variants.

summary: shared_mutex (C++17), shared_timed_mutex (C++14), shared_lock. Reader-writer locking.
condition_variable, condition_variable_any, cv_status enum, notify_all_at_thread_exit. The wait/notify primitive for thread coordination.
future / shared_future / promise / packaged_task, async, launch enum, future_status / future_error / future_errc / future_category. Asynchronous result delivery.
counting_semaphore<LeastMaxValue> + binary_semaphore alias. C++20 acquire / release / try_acquire / try_acquire_for / try_acquire_until.
blockers: <atomic> for the counter; <chrono> for the timed variants.

summary: std::latch. C++20 single-use down-counter — count_down / wait / try_wait / arrive_and_wait.
std::barrier<CompletionFunction>. C++20 reusable barrier — arrive / wait / arrive_and_wait / arrive_and_drop, with an optional completion phase.
stop_token / stop_source / stop_callback / nostopstate_t. Cooperative cancellation primitive. Anchors jthread's stop API.

execution policies (sequenced_policy, parallel_policy, parallel_unsequenced_policy, unsequenced_policy + the seq / par / par_unseq / unseq instances). The hook for parallel-algorithm overloads in <algorithm> and <numeric>.
blockers: Platform thread pool / TBB / OpenMP integration for the par_* policies.

summary: hazard_pointer / hazard_pointer_obj_base. C++26 lock-free reclamation primitive.
rcu_obj_base / rcu_domain. C++26 read-copy-update synchronisation primitive.
std::generator<Ref, V, Allocator>. C++23 coroutine-based input range view. Anchor for the deferred <ranges>::generator dependency.

C++26 std::linalg namespace — BLAS-style dense linear algebra (matrix_*, vector_*, the operation tags + the free functions add / scale / scaled / conjugated / transposed / hermitian_transposed / etc.). Layered on <mdspan>.
is_debugger_present, breakpoint, breakpoint_if_debugging. C++26 debugger interaction primitives.
std::text_encoding. C++26 identification of named character encodings (mostly IANA names).
blockers: <string_view>; embedded encoding registry (could share data with <format>'s Unicode width tables).

summary: assert macro. Toggles on NDEBUG. Trivial passthrough to the C <assert.h>.

isalnum / isalpha / isblank / iscntrl / isdigit / isgraph / islower / isprint / ispunct / isspace / isupper / isxdigit / tolower / toupper. Locale-affected in C but always-C-locale in re_std unless wired through <locale>.
errno macro + the E* error number constants. Pure passthrough to <errno.h>.
fenv_t, fexcept_t, feclearexcept / fegetexceptflag / feraiseexcept / fesetexceptflag / fetestexcept, fegetround / fesetround, fegetenv / fesetenv / feholdexcept / feupdateenv. FP environment access.

PARTLY AVAILABLE: the PRI* / SCN* format macros already reach C++98 through dstdint.h, which <cstdint>'s face includes -- with the msvcrt.dll handling MinGW needs (I64 for ll, no hh), and the 8-bit scanf formats left out below C++11, where hh does not exist. REMAINING: imaxdiv_t, imaxabs / imaxdiv, strtoimax / strtoumax, wcstoimax / wcstoumax, and the abs / div overloads C++ adds when intmax_t is an extended integer type. The C workbook's <inttypes.h> sheet tracks the same functions; one C implementation would serve both.
locale-related — setlocale, localeconv, lconv struct, LC_* category macros. Passthrough to <locale.h>. Distinct from <locale>.

abs / fabs / fmod / remainder / remquo / fma / fmin / fmax / fdim / nan / exp / exp2 / expm1 / log / log10 / log2 / log1p / pow / sqrt / cbrt / hypot / sin / cos / tan / asin / acos / atan / atan2 / sinh / cosh / tanh / asinh / acosh / atanh / erf / erfc / lgamma / tgamma / ceil / floor / trunc / round / lround / llround / nearbyint / rint / lrint / llrint / frexp / ldexp / modf / scalbn / scalbln / ilogb / logb / nextafter / nexttoward / copysign / FP classification (fpclassify / isfinite / isinf / isnan / isnormal / signbit) / FP comparison (isgreater / isgreaterequal / isless / islessequal / islessgreater / isunordered). Pure passthrough but enormous surface.
jmp_buf, setjmp / longjmp. Pure passthrough — discouraged in C++ (skips destructors).
sig_atomic_t, SIG_* macros, signal / raise. Pure passthrough.
va_list / va_start / va_arg / va_end / va_copy. Pure passthrough.

FILE, fpos_t, EOF / NULL / BUFSIZ / FILENAME_MAX / FOPEN_MAX / L_tmpnam / TMP_MAX, stdin/stdout/stderr, fopen / freopen / fclose / fflush / setbuf / setvbuf, fread / fwrite, fgetc / fputc / fgets / fputs / fgetpos / fsetpos / fseek / ftell / rewind / ferror / feof / clearerr / perror, printf family, scanf family, remove / rename / tmpfile / tmpnam. memchr / memcmp / memcpy / memmove / memset, strcpy / strncpy / strcat / strncat / strcmp / strncmp / strchr / strrchr / strspn / strcspn / strpbrk / strstr / strtok / strlen, strcoll / strxfrm, strerror, NULL. Pure passthrough.
clock_t, time_t, tm struct, timespec (C++17), CLOCKS_PER_SEC, clock / time / difftime / mktime / asctime / ctime / gmtime / localtime / strftime / timespec_get (C++17). Pure passthrough.
char16_t / char32_t (C++11), mbrtoc16 / c16rtomb / mbrtoc32 / c32rtomb. Multi-byte to char16_t/char32_t conversion.

wchar_t, wint_t, mbstate_t, WCHAR_MIN/MAX, WEOF, the wide-char string functions (wcscpy / wcsncpy / wcscat / etc.), the wide stdio (fwide / fgetwc / fputwc / fgetws / fputws / fwprintf / fwscanf / etc.), wcstod / wcstof / wcstold / wcstol / wcstoll / wcstoul / wcstoull, mbsinit / btowc / wctob / mbrlen / mbrtowc / wcrtomb / mbsrtowcs / wcsrtombs.

wint_t, wctype_t, wctrans_t, WEOF, iswalnum / iswalpha / iswblank / iswcntrl / iswdigit / iswgraph / iswlower / iswprint / iswpunct / iswspace / iswupper / iswxdigit, iswctype / wctype, towlower / towupper, towctrans / wctrans.

C atomic operations. C++23 added this header for C-source-compat scenarios; explicitly no <cstdatomic> equivalent. Mostly mirrors <atomic> semantics but with C-syntax (atomic_int + atomic_load / atomic_store).
C bit-manipulation functions (stdc_leading_zeros / stdc_count_ones / etc.). C++26; no <cstdbit> equivalent.
Checked integer arithmetic (ckd_add / ckd_sub / ckd_mul). C++26; no <cstdckdint> equivalent.

C++ equivalent of <iso646.h>. Meaningless in C++ since the alternative tokens (and / or / not / etc.) are language keywords. DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++20. Empty file in re_std for C++11-17 compat.
C++ equivalent of <stdalign.h>. Meaningless in C++ since alignas / alignof are language keywords. DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++20.
C++ equivalent of <stdbool.h>. Meaningless in C++ since bool / true / false are language keywords. DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++20.
Re-included <complex> for C compatibility. DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++20. Pure forwarding header — no actual content.
Re-included <ccomplex> + <cmath> for C compatibility (the C99 tgmath.h type-generic math). DEPRECATED in C++17, REMOVED in C++20.
